A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GenRM research, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–E. Corresponding appendix content is identical apart from page numbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original algorithmic-reasoning, GSM8K, and MATH experiments, including verifier comparisons, ablations, scaling analyses, and qualitative examples.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds MMLU mathematics evaluations in Table 1 and Figure 7.

M1.justification: The verification objectives, joint generation training, CoT generation, and probability averaging remain unchanged. Section 3.3 clarifies that reference solutions are excluded from verifier finetuning; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluations on MMLU elementary mathematics, high-school mathematics, college mathematics, and abstract algebra using grade-school-trained verifiers. This extends the existing mathematical generalization coverage to college-level subjects while retaining all previous tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments. The new MMLU comparisons reuse existing comparators: discriminative RM and base-model performance in Table 1, plus self-consistency in Figure 7.

E3.justification: The added college-mathematics experiment specifies Best-of-32 evaluation with Gemini 1.0 Pro solutions and varying verification-rationale counts. Figure 1 also replaces the normalized oracle-gap summary with starting-to-final accuracy summaries. Existing training and evaluation settings are retained.

E4.justification: v3 Figure 7 adds a sensitivity analysis of verification-rationale count on MMLU college mathematics, extending the existing GSM8K compute-scaling analysis. Earlier ablations and the appendix case studies remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Sampling multiple verification rationales remains an inference procedure, not uncertainty estimation across experimental runs.

E6.justification: New Table 1 reports discriminative RM versus GenRM-CoT accuracies of 90.6% versus 91.1%, 74.8% versus 76.1%, 53.0% versus 56.1%, and 50.0% versus 53.5% across the four MMLU subjects. Figure 7 adds college-mathematics comparisons and scaling results. These are new evaluations; existing benchmark results are retained.

T1.justification: Figure 1 removes the explicit definition Delta = (GenRM-CoT − Disc-RM)/(Pass@N − Disc-RM) and reuses Delta for starting-to-final accuracy summaries. This is a limited mathematical-definition change; the method equations and other mathematical content remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract adds a specific MMLU abstract-algebra generalization claim, reporting 37.9% base-model accuracy versus 53.5% with GenRM-CoT, and replaces the aggregate 16–40% statement with task-specific figures. The central methodological contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 4.3 changes its interpretation from better scaling behavior than discriminative RMs to better performance across model sizes. Section 3.3 also explicitly explains why reference-assisted data generation does not create a train/test input mismatch.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly states that reference solutions condition synthetic-rationale generation but are omitted during verifier finetuning. This improves implementation clarity without demonstrating a setting change. Appendix hyperparameters, filtering instructions, prompts, and data-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds Hendrycks et al. (2020), the MMLU reference. The substantive related-work comparisons and positioning against earlier verifier approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized edits revise the abstract, expand preliminary explanations of LLM-as-a-Judge, clarify synthetic-rationale training, and update the experimental narrative, publication header, and author contributions. The overall section structure and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 1 and the two-panel Figure 7, revises Figure 1 annotations and axis ticks, and relocates or renumbers existing figures. Figure 9 adds an axis-baseline statement despite retaining the original plotted scales. Appendix displays are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The MMLU evaluations broaden support for easy-to-hard generalization, and Section 3.3 makes reference-solution handling clearer. These limited gains outweigh a new caption inconsistency: Figure 9 claims axes start at base-generator Pass@1, but its GSM8K axis starts near 88%, whereas the reported baseline is 73%. The core method and earlier evidence remain unchanged.
